A1.justification: Both 35-page PDFs describe LatentMAS and include the main paper and Appendices A–K. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of their text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark experiments measuring accuracy, token usage, and inference time, plus alignment analyses, ablations, and debug-mode validation in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark experiments and supplementary analyses, including the empirical outcomes in Tables 1–8.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same latent thought generation, input-output alignment, KV-cache transfer, and final text decoding procedures. The debug-mode procedure in Appendix F is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, AIME24, AIME25, GPQA-Diamond, MedQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MBPP-Plus, and HumanEval-Plus. Sequential and hierarchical scenarios and the supplementary evaluation coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same Single and TextMAS comparators, including the appendix comparisons and hybrid variants in Table 7. The newly cited works in v4 are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Model backbones, agent arrangements, latent-step budgets, decoding settings, evaluation metrics, and answer-checking procedures remain identical in Section 4 and Appendix C. Supplementary analyses retain their sample sizes and protocols.

E4.justification: The alignment, latent-depth, representation-diversity, final-agent token, and hybrid ablation analyses are unchanged. The debug validation in Appendix F and case studies in Appendices I–J are also retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean performance over three independent runs in Section 4. No changes occur in run information, uncertainty reporting, or statistical procedures, including the appendix debug analysis.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–8 and plotted results in Figures 1 and 4–11 are identical. Qualitative findings and case-study outputs are also unchanged; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The expressiveness, information-preservation, and complexity theorems retain their statements, assumptions, and proofs. The alignment theorem and derivations in Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same training-free latent collaboration, expressiveness, lossless-transfer, accuracy, and efficiency claims. The related-work edits do not redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations of efficiency, alignment, diversity, error propagation, and debug validity are unchanged. Appendix G retains the same shared-layer-shape assumption and discussion of extending the framework to heterogeneous agents.

D1.justification: Implementation details, software backends, hyperparameters, hardware, evaluation instructions, and Appendix K's prompt templates are unchanged. Project/code access information and dataset access references are also retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds A Survey on Latent Reasoning, Mixture of Thoughts, and Bridging Hidden States in Vision-Language Models to the literature discussion and bibliography. Section 1 moves Zheng et al. (2025) from single-model latent reasoning to cross-model information exchange and changes 'across two models' to 'across models'. These are limited refinements to prior-work coverage and characterization.

P1.justification: Localized wording and citation edits affect a prior-work paragraph in Section 1 and the latent-reasoning paragraph in Appendix H, including shorter positioning prose. The section organization and remaining narrative are unchanged; the arXiv version/date stamp is updated.

P2.justification: The added references reflow bibliography entries across pages 10–13, with limited paragraph line-wrap changes elsewhere. All figures, tables, captions, and their placements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 1 now classifies Zheng et al. as cross-model communication, matching its treatment in Section 6, and removes the narrower 'two models' description. Together with the added references in Appendix H, this modestly improves the consistency and coverage of the literature discussion. The technical arguments, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information are unchanged.
